title: Positive elements of a split-real rational algebra are sums of squares
statement:
Let $C$ be a commutative unital $\mathbf Q$-algebra, meaning a commutative ring with a unital homomorphism $\mathbf Q\to C$. Suppose its underlying $\mathbf Q$-vector space has a finite basis. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer and let
$$\rho:C\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R^d$$
be an isomorphism of unital $\mathbf R$-algebras, with coordinatewise operations on $\mathbf R^d$ and scalar tensor product as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If $x\in C$ satisfies $\rho(x\otimes1)_i>0$ for every $1\leq i\leq d$, then there are an integer $r\geq1$ and elements $q_1,\ldots,q_r\in C$ such that
$$x=\sum_{j=1}^r q_j^2.$$
The zero algebra and $d=0$ are allowed. The squares and the equality are in $C$, not merely in its scalar extension to $\mathbf R$.

source.place: Agent algebraic auxiliary for the abelian endomorphism-span input; the split-real algebra setting is motivated by II §1, proof of Lemma 1.3, pp.77–78. The sum-of-squares theorem is an agent argument, written in the report, not an assertion attributed to that lemma.

proof.text: Choose a rational basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $C$. Its coordinate functionals $\lambda_j:C\to\mathbf Q$ extend to real linear maps $\widetilde\lambda_j:C\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R\to\mathbf R$ by $\widetilde\lambda_j(c\otimes t)=\lambda_j(c)t$, using the bilinear universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On pure tensors the basis identity gives $c\otimes t=\sum_j(b_j\otimes1)\lambda_j(c)t$, and $\widetilde\lambda_i(b_j\otimes1)=\delta_{ij}$. Thus $b_j\otimes1$ is a real basis. If $n=0$, the rational basis already gives $C=0$; take $r=1,q_1=0$. Henceforth $n>0$.

source.place: Agent Gram-matrix argument for the algebraic auxiliary; Milne II §1 Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 is motivation only, not a source asserting sums of squares. See report.md.

proof.text: Put $D=C\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R$ and $x_i=\rho(x\otimes1)_i>0$. Let $e_i=\rho^{-1}(\delta_i)$ for the coordinate vectors $\delta_i$ of $\mathbf R^d$, and write $e_i=\sum_a t_{ai}(b_a\otimes1)$ with $t_i=(t_{ai})_a\in\mathbf R^n$. Since $\rho$ is an algebra isomorphism, $e_i^2=e_i$ and $x\otimes1=\sum_i x_i e_i$; since it is a linear isomorphism, the $t_i$ form a real basis. Define the symmetric matrix $G_{ab}=\sum_i x_i t_{ai}t_{bi}$. For $z\ne0$, some $\sum_a z_at_{ai}$ is nonzero (otherwise $z$ is orthogonal to a spanning family and hence to itself), so $\sum_{a,b}z_aG_{ab}z_b=\sum_i x_i(\sum_a z_at_{ai})^2>0$. Also, by expansion of the squares, $\sum_{a,b}G_{ab}(b_ab_b\otimes1)=\sum_i x_ie_i^2=x\otimes1$.

proof.text: Define a rational linear map $L:\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbf Q)\to\mathbf Q^n$ by taking the coordinates in the basis $(b_a)$ of $\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}b_ab_b$, and let $\xi\in\mathbf Q^n$ be the coordinates of $x$. The multiplication structure constants of $C$ in this rational basis are rational, so the real map with these same coefficients takes $G$ to $\xi$, by the preceding displayed equality and the extended coordinate functionals. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-positive-definite-feasibility] with $m=n$, this $L$, and $b=\xi$. It gives a rational symmetric $H$ with $L(H)=\xi$ and with positive definite real image. The exact rational equality $L(H)=\xi$ says $\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}b_ab_b=x$ in $C$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-rational-positive-definite-gram] to $H$. Obtain $r\geq0$ and $v_k\in\mathbf Q^n$ with $H_{ab}=\sum_{k=1}^r(v_k)_a(v_k)_b$. Set $q_k=\sum_a(v_k)_ab_a\in C$. Distributivity and commutativity give
$$\sum_kq_k^2=\sum_{a,b}\left(\sum_k(v_k)_a(v_k)_b\right)b_ab_b=\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}b_ab_b=x.$$
If necessary append the zero element as one additional summand, ensuring that the number of summands is at least one. All coefficients and all $q_k$ lie in $\mathbf Q$ and $C$, respectively; the last equality is already in $C$.
